chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Louis Armstrong at Freedomland and the autographed kimono photo
summary: Lu tells how Louis scolded her for sending Jack Bradley to ask for an autograph instead of asking him herself.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Speaking of Louis, remember when they had Freedomland in New York...?
Well, Jack Bradley... You know Jack Bradley.
Well, Jack Bradley took some pictures of Louis, and the pictures were him in a kimono. Not just Louis, he got a hundred people in them. So he gave me a couple of these pictures.

So Louis was out in Freedomland. So Jack said, "Well, let's go out and see Louis tonight." I said, "Okay." Then we had a (?) to go and see Louis. So I had the picture with me, you know. Except he was in a kimono in the picture. I didn't want to go ask Louis to autograph the picture, you know. So I had been in his dressing room, talking to him and everything. When we came out, Jack said, "You got the picture autographed?" I said, "Unh-uh. I don't want to ask Louis to..." I said, "You go and ask Louis to autograph the picture for me."
So Jack went and asked him, and he said to Jack, "Where's..." He called me Don't You Feel My Leg. He said, "Where is Don't You Feel My Leg?" Jack said, "She's

outside." So he came to me and said, "Come in." So I went in, and he said, "Now, why did you send Jack to ask me to autograph those pictures for you. Why didn't you come in here and ask me yourself?" I said, "Well, you know, he took the (?) picture." I felt kind of ashamed then. He said, "Don't you ask him to ask me nothin'." He said, "Anything you want from me, you come ask me. You don't ask nobody. You come and ask me." So I said to him, "Can I hang this picture up?" He said, "Hang it wherever you want! Hang it in your living room if you want to. Do what you want with it." I said, "Would it be all right?" Because he said, "Yeah, it would be all right!" But he said, "Now, don't you do that no more. You come to me. You don't send nobody to ask me nothing. You come and ask me." I said "Okay."
That's a nice story. That's the kind of man he was.
